Gold rules backtest, 5 years: 20 Nov 2021 to 20 Nov 2026 (US Eastern time)

Every gold rule in the project (TA Section 34 and other TA/KD gold items, the 2026 document's gold section, your Sun notes U1–U4), recomputed with the Swiss-Ephemeris engine (Lahiri, mean node, whole-sign drishti) and scored against COMEX gold futures daily closes (Yahoo Finance GC=F continuous front month). Gold went from 1,851.6 (19 Nov 2021) to 3,539.0 (20 Nov 2026), +91.1%, peaking at 5,318.4 on 29 Jan 2026 (largest one-day fall -10.8%).

Rules checked (U2, U4 split by planet)48
Rules that fired42
Scored occurrences696
Worked308
Failed279
Flat (<0.5%)109
Hit rate52%
Rules: worked / mixed / failed10 / 16 / 13

Key findings

  1. Overall. 308 of 587 decided occurrences worked (52%), against 54% expected by chance from the base rates of those same occurrences (p = 0.767 for doing this well or better by luck). On the 204 trading days when more bearish than bullish gold rules were active, gold moved +0.06% on average over the next 5 days (52% up); on the 910 bullish-majority days, +0.46% (60% up). Correlation of the daily net count with the next 5-day move: +0.049.
  2. Statistically clear results (p < 0.05 against the base rate):
    • None of the rules beat chance at that level.
  3. What worked (most decided occurrences first):

    • Moon darshan on Saturday (gold) (Bearish): 4 of 7 worked (57% vs base 43%), average move +0.30% in the stated direction; p = 0.358; right in 2 of 4 years with a result

  5. Why bullish rules failed. Conditions clearly more common when they failed: Jupiter sharing a sign with Rahu / Ketu / Mars / Saturn (19% of failures vs 9% of successes). More common when they worked: Jupiter on the Sun at the start (20% of failures vs 32% of successes).
  6. Why bearish rules failed. Conditions clearly more common when they failed: Jupiter on the Sun at the start (41% of failures vs 16% of successes); Sun's nakshatra lord against the rule (user U1/U3) (40% of failures vs 22% of successes); Mars on the Sun at the start (38% of failures vs 22% of successes); A planet stations inside the interval (53% of failures vs 37% of successes). More common when they worked: none stood out.
  7. Biggest single miss: the late-January 2026 crash (2026-01-26 → 2026-02-02, -8.5%, including the −10.8% day on 30 Jan after the 29 Jan peak). Gold rules active: 6 bullish, 2 bearish. Sky: Sun in Shravana (lord Moon), Capricorn; Mercury with Sun, Venus with Sun, Mars with Sun; Jupiter Gemini Punarvasu R; 29 Jan: Mercury conjunction Venus in Capricorn; 31 Jan-01 Feb: Venus combust. The Sun, Mercury, Venus and Mars were all in Capricorn (Mars exalted), Venus was about to combust and Jupiter was retrograde. No rule in the set describes a four-planet stellium on the Sun or a Venus combustion, and none of your Sun rules treats Mars, Mercury or Venus crowding the Sun as negative.
  8. March 2026 (2026-03-17 → 2026-03-24, -12.1%): bearish rules active: Saturn in Uttara Bhadrapada (Brihat Samhita 10.17); Sun in a Saturn or Rahu nakshatra (user note); U4 - Saturn with / aspecting the Sun; 9 bullish rules active at the same time. Sky: Sun in Uttara Bhadrapada (lord Saturn), Pisces; Moon with Sun, Venus with Sun, Saturn with Sun.
  9. The 15 biggest 5-day falls: bearish rules outnumbered bullish ones in 1 of them; in the rest the rule set leaned bullish going into the fall (it leans bullish on 72% of all trading days, so a bullish majority by itself carries little information). 2026-03-17 -12.1% (9:3); 2026-11-13 -8.9% (5:3); 2026-06-04 -8.7% (2:3); 2026-01-26 -8.5% (6:2); 2026-06-16 -7.9% (7:2); 2025-10-20 -7.8% (7:1); 2026-08-25 -6.3% (5:2); 2025-05-07 -6.0% (8:2).
  10. The 15 biggest 5-day rises: bullish rules outnumbered bearish ones in 13 of them.
  11. How far to trust this. 5 years give the frequent rules (Sun contacts, new moons, vedha, darshan) enough occurrences to judge; 20 rules still have fewer than 5 decided occurrences, and their records stay anecdotal. A rule that is right in most individual years is more trustworthy than one whose total comes from a single year; check the per-year columns.

How each occurrence was scored

  • Entry = the last daily close before the event (events at or after 17:00 ET count from the next session; panchang day-rules from that day's open).
  • Windows of 3 days or more (a planet in a nakshatra or sign, Sun contacts…) are scored from entry to the last close inside the window, clipped to the backtest period. Instants and short windows (new moon, darshan, rise/set, ingress, vedha starts) are scored on the 5-trading-day move; 1-, 3- and 10-day moves are shown as a sensitivity check.
  • Moves under ±0.5% are FLAT. Rules whose verdict is Mixed or Neutral (both vedha kinds at once; the Indian festival-demand dates) are listed but not scored.
  • Hit rate = worked ÷ (worked + failed); flat occurrences are left out of both.
  • Base rate = the hit rate a rule would get by chance: among all windows of the same length in the same backtest year that moved more than 0.5%, the share that moved the rule's way. Over the whole period a 5-day window that moved went up 56% of the time, so a bullish rule needs to beat 56% and a bearish rule 44% to show any edge. Using each year's own base rate means a bullish rule gets no credit just for firing in a rising year.
  • Rule verdict: Worked = hit rate at least 10 points above its base rate and the average move went the stated way; Failed = at least 10 points below and the average move went the wrong way; otherwise Mixed. p-value = the chance of doing at least this well by luck at the base rate (one-sided binomial); green if below 0.05, red if the rule did significantly worse than chance. The per-year columns show worked/decided in each Nov–Nov year, so a rule that only worked in one year stands out.

Why rules failed: what keeps showing up

Each condition is checked for every failed occurrence and every occurrence that worked. A condition only helps explain failures if it is clearly more common among the failures; Sun contacts are read at the start of the occurrence. These are pointers, not proof of cause.

Which sky factors were present in the biggest moves?
